source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1938, p. 13 ("Contests in Derry wards: Nationalists opposed")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed (News-Letter, 6 May 1938: Waterside nominees and North aldermen returned unopposed on nomination day)

note: First election on the new wards made by an Order of 1937, which cut Londonderry Corporation from five wards and 40 members to three wards and 20: North and South each two aldermen and six councillors, Waterside one alderman and three councillors. Whole council elected; nominations Thursday 5 May, poll Monday 16 May 1938, results declared 17 May. The Waterside members and the North aldermen were returned unopposed; the Unionists won 12 of the 20 seats (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 17 and 18 May 1938). Wilton, M.C., was Mayor; both were Unionist nominees. Returned unopposed.
